title: Flying Saucer Goes on Sale in China: A Two-Person Craft Capable of Landing on Water and Land | AVA
excerpt: A Chinese company has launched sales of an electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft resembling a quot;flying saucerquot; in the city of Yiwu; the vehicle is designed to carry one or two passengers and is intended for tourism and aerial displays.
content:
Afghan Voice Agency (AVA) – International Service: Developed by the Shenzhen-based company "Xihang," this eVTOL aircraft features a transparent, spherical 360-degree cabin. Utilizing vertical take-off and landing technology, it requires no runway and is capable of taking off and landing on both water and land.

This "flying saucer" reaches a maximum altitude of approximately 30 meters and has a reported flight time of about 15 minutes. Equipped with an automatic flight control system and a six-propeller design, it can withstand wind speeds up to Level 5.

Priced at 800,000 Chinese yuan, the aircraft is primarily intended by the manufacturer for low-altitude tourism, sightseeing in recreational areas, and aerial performances. Reports indicate that the product has already secured a major order worth nearly 120 million yuan.

According to Chinese media reports, the aircraft has received a special flight permit from the Civil Aviation Administration of China. However, given its limited altitude and flight duration, the vehicle is currently intended mainly for recreational and tourism purposes and is not a substitute for conventional passenger aircraft.
